s1.syndrome_frame: Tooth pain with abnormal root canal morphology and periapical radiolucency
salient_findings: Spontaneous dull pain during root canal therapy
Tender response to percussion
No response to cold or electric pulp tests
Periapical radiolucency at apex of DB root
C-shaped canal morphology in P root
key_facts: Patient is a 26-year-old female
Referred for root canal retreatment of tooth #17
Tooth sealed with temporary filling material
Tender in response to percussion
No response to cold or electric pulp tests
Radiopaque filling material visible in coronal third of canal
Periapical radiolucency present at apex of DB root
C-shaped canal morphology in P root
Two different canal orifices in coronal third of P canal
Canals joined to form C-shaped ribbon-like pattern in middle third
Two P canals joined to one foramen in apical part

shortlist.label: Chronic Apical Periodontitis
shortlist.why_kept: Tender in response to percussion and periapical radiolucency

shortlist.label: Acute Apical Periodontitis
shortlist.why_kept: Spontaneous dull pain and no response to cold or electric pulp tests

shortlist.label: Periapical Cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Periapical radiolucency present at apex of DB root

shortlist.label: C-Shaped Canal Syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's tooth is tender in response to percussion and has a periapical radiolucency, which are indicative of an acute inflammatory response, consistent with Acute Apical Periodontitis.

rejected.label: Chronic Apical Periodontitis
rejected.why: The presence of spontaneous dull pain and tenderness to percussion suggests an acute rather than chronic condition.

rejected.label: Periapical Cyst
rejected.why: There is no mention of a cystic lesion or a well-defined radiolucency that would be characteristic of a periapical cyst.

rejected.label: C-Shaped Canal Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has a C-shaped canal morphology, this is a anatomical variation rather than a diagnosis, and does not directly explain the patient's symptoms.

rejected.label: Root Canal Treatment Failure
rejected.why: The patient is being referred for root canal retreatment, but the primary issue appears to be an acute apical periodontitis rather than a failure of the root canal treatment itself.

rejected.label: Chronic Apical Periodontitis
rejected.why: The symptoms and signs presented are more consistent with an acute condition rather than a chronic one
